New TTC Board chair says he’s concerned about allegations surrounding CEO
items.summary: Newly appointed TTC Board Chair Paul Ainslie says recent questions around the commission’s leadership and spending are “very concerning” to him and he intends to follow up on them in his new role.

items.title: More cadets, more money, less training: Military defends controversial suspension
items.summary: The second-in-command of Canada's military stood behind the decision to suspend most cadet training in various parts of the country, suggesting the program is swamped by an increase in participation and struggling not to blow its annual budget.

items.title: Officer says Francique 'threw wrench' in police arrest plan, inquest hears
items.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Black man shot in the head by police heard from the supervisory officer on scene that day that his team would not have done anything differently as they were on-site to complete what they believed would be a routine arrest.

items.title: Experts cite child suicide, trafficking as they urge MPs to pass digital safety bill
items.summary: A pediatrician who is urging the Liberal government to quickly pass its digital safety bill says social media and AI chatbots amount to a massive, unregulated experiment on children’s brains.

items.title: Hong Kong police hunt man suspected of stealing cameras, lenses worth HK$1.9 million
items.summary: Hong Kong police are searching for a man suspected of stealing 61 cameras and 55 lenses worth nearly HK$1.9 million (US$242,300) from a shop in Causeway Bay, the South China Morning Post has learned.
